title: Laying out the body: veil, flowers and candles
summary: Rene describes the veil, where flowers were placed and the three candles representing God, Father and Son, now replaced by electric bulbs.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers

blocks.x: Oh, back to the funeral. When they have a man laid out, what is in the old days on this cot deal, rolling cot, what would they have around him?

Well they wouldn't have nothing more than a sort of a veil over him, you know. That's all kind of flies and things, you know. They have a veil over them and some people would have, you know, bring flowers or something. Well they would set the flowers right at the head or at the feet, you know. They wouldn't set it in front because people walk towards the front and different people, because if a cattley walks in there, he's going to lead and make a prayer, see. The Baptist comes, he's got to stand up and pray, you understand? So they use that, they keep that front clear.
But did you ever see a clock at a deal like this, you know, in the old days, marking an hour of death?
People didn't have that kind of money. See, it's farming fashion now. Nothing takes a dot it.
He puts a clock on it.
And he's getting the money, yeah, sure. You see all that, that's expensive.
What about candles around the body? Did they have candles in those days?
Oh yeah, they used to have candles. Still had, that always was, them three candles.
And what are the three candles?
